Q: Flutter: Continuous notification sound + vibration works in foreground but not when app is closed (using flutter_foreground_task) A:

Yes — what you’re seeing is expected Android behavior.

Your implementation is mostly correct, but modern Android heavily restricts background execution when the app is terminated, especially for audio playback. The issue is not Flutter or FCM — it’s Android background launch + audio policy + OEM power restrictions.

Below is what’s actually happening and the correct approach.

Why sound doesn’t play when app is killed

  1. FCM delivery works

    • onMessageReceived() can fire in killed state for high-priority data messages.

    • So your service start request is valid.

  2. But Android limits what can start from background
    Since Android 12+:

    • Background services cannot freely start audio playback

    • Foreground services started from background are allowed, but media playback may still be suppressed

    • Doze mode + OEM battery managers can delay audio output

    • Audio focus may not be granted instantly

  3. If the user force-stopped the app
    → Nothing will run. FCM will not launch your process at all.

    This is a hard Android rule.

The real root issue

Your approach is trying to simulate an alarm app, but Android treats:

  • Notifications

  • Foreground services

  • Alarm apps

as different execution classes

Swiggy/Zomato style alerts are implemented using alarm-style notifications, not just MediaPlayer in a service.

Correct approach for alarm-style incoming order alerts

You should combine three Android mechanisms:

Use Full-Screen Intent notification

This is what ride apps and delivery apps use.

It:

  • Wakes the screen

  • Bypasses background limits

  • Gets immediate audio permission

  • Works from killed state

    Your notification builder must include:

.setCategory(NotificationCompat.CATEGORY_CALL) 
.setPriority(NotificationCompat.PRIORITY_MAX)
.setFullScreenIntent(pendingIntent, true)

Use CATEGORY_CALL or CATEGORY_ALARM.

Play sound through the Notification itself

Do NOT rely only on MediaPlayer.

Instead:

.setSound(alarmUri)
.setVibrate(pattern)

Android treats notification sounds differently from service audio.

This is why alarm apps work even when killed.

Only use ForegroundService as backup

Start the service after notification triggers.

Let notification wake device → then service continues looping sound.

This ordering matters.

Recommended architecture

Step 1 — FCM arrives
→ Build full-screen alarm notification with sound

Step 2 — Notification wakes device
→ User sees order UI instantly

Step 3 — Start foreground service
→ Continue looping sound/vibration until user acts

This is exactly how:

  • Swiggy driver app

  • Uber driver

  • Foodpanda courier

implement incoming orders.

Important Android Manifest additions

You likely need:

<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WAKE_LOCK"/>

For Android 14+ also declare foreground service type:

<service
    android:name=".OrderAlertForegroundService"
    android:foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback" />

Final Recommendation

Yes — you should switch to:

✔ Full-screen notification
✔ Alarm category notification sound
✔ Service only as secondary loop
✔ Avoid relying solely on MediaPlayer

That is the correct Android-approved way to build persistent order alerts.

Q: Git debugging - "error: could not delete references: cannot lock ref" "File exists" A:

I had the same problem when doing git fetch -apt, and my issue is the one tracked in (still open):

  • https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/issues/5378
  • https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/issues/5900

Considered that re-cloning is safer than manipulating .git folder internals, you can still proceed with the following solution that worked for me on windows; it's an hard reset the pack-refs:

  1. Make sure everything is committed or stashed.

  2. Remove all the packed-refs folder:

    Remove-Item .git\packed-refs -Force

  3. Re-fetch and rebuild the references:

    git fetch --all --prune
git pack-refs --all

  4. Move into the correct branch where you want to be:

    git switch main

  5. Verify everything is correct:

    git fsck --full --strict

  6. If you want to clean up everything and clean dangling commits normalize everything use:

    git gc --prune=now

After step 6 fsck everything was perfect for me.
Still remember that re-cloning is the safest option if you're unsure.
